question_type: log growth rate of a bank-reported year-end liabilities series between two calendar years, each endpoint revised across later issues

opus_path.decision: Series is the Capital Movements 'Total liabilities to all foreigners' row in Table CM-I-1 (bank-reported, millions, position at end of period); 'end of calendar year' = the table's 'Calendar Year YYYY' column; log growth = 100*ln(V2012/V2002); default vintage = latest published revision because no issue is pinned.
Found CM-I-1 and its header in the March 2013 issue by grepping the exact row label.

Followed the Dec-2012/CY2012 cell through the 2013_03, 2013_06, 2013_09 and 2013_12 issues, reading each header; established that CM-I tables stop after 2013_12, so the 'Calendar Year 2012 r' column there is final.

Followed the CY2002 cell through 2003_03 (Dec p), 2003_06, 2003_09 (Dec r), 2003_12 (first 'Calendar Year 2002 r'), 2004_03, 2004_06, 2004_09, reading each header; saw that 2004_03 still labels its first column 'Calendar Year 2002 r' with a further revision, which then stays unchanged; confirmed with a corpus-wide count that the value recurs through Chart CM-A in 2007_03 with no later change.
Cross-checked that the CM-I-1 total equals the CM-I-2 grand total and the Chart CM-A grand total in the same issues (right series).
Computed 100*ln ratio in calc.py at full precision; logged the alternative vintage pairs and the simple percent change as rejected alternatives.
Independent reviewer re-opened both source line ranges, re-ran the later-printing greps and recomputed; verdict confirmed (vintage ambiguity only).

opus_key_moves: Walked the CY2002 cell forward through every quarterly issue and read each issue's column header, so it saw that 2004_03/06/09 still carry a 'Calendar Year 2002' column (a second restatement) after the Dec 2003 'Calendar Year 2002 r' printing.
Established finality by grep-counting later occurrences (value stable 2004_03 through 2007_03) and by confirming CM-I tables end with the 2013_12 issue.
Cross-checked the row against CM-I-2 and Chart CM-A totals in the same issue.

none.right_arms_note: Started from the 2003_03 preliminary cell ([34]-[36]) but asked at [37] whether later bulletins revised it; an FTS query for 'Dec 2002' surfaced 2004_03/2004_06, it read the 2004_06 header ('Calendar Year 2002') at [40]-[42], then checked 2003_12 [47] and 2004_03 [49] before committing the latest revision.

first_divergence.what_glm_did: At [41] grepped the total row in every 2003 and 2004 issue (row lines only, no headers); at [43] read headers only for 2003_03 and 2003_12; at [44] asserted, without opening it, that the first column of the 2004_03 table is calendar 2003, concluded the Dec 2003 issue is the last printing of CY2002, and used that intermediate restatement.
first_divergence.what_opus_did: Read the CM-I-1 header in 2004_03, 2004_06 and 2004_09 (all 'Calendar Year 2002', r in 2004_03) and took the later restatement that stays stable through 2007_03.
first_divergence.why_glm_went_that_way: [44] THINK raised the right question ('Could be 2004_03 first col 2002?') and answered it by assumption ('Actually 2004_03 first col ... (calendar 2003)'), apparently expecting the annual column to roll forward by the March issue. The tell-tale pattern in its own [41] output (same first-column value in 2004_03, 2004_06, 2004_09, changing only in 2004_12) was not interpreted.
first_divergence.consequence: CY2002 endpoint about 0.5% below the final revision, giving a log-growth answer about 0.6% too high (within_1pct, strict wrong).

secondary_errors.note: The pre-commit vintage re-check at [47] was applied only to the 2012 endpoint; the 2002 endpoint was not re-examined.

saw_correct_evidence.where: [41] output prints the 2004_03, 2004_06 and 2004_09 'Total liabilities to all foreigners' rows whose first cell is the final CY2002 revision; only the header line was missing.

adapter_context.relevant_item: Procedure self-check 1 (name the vintage and compare with the latest bulletin carrying the row); L-defense-table3-annual-vintage ('match the column by its header, not by position'); Open-questions note 'grep the row forward and use the latest vintage'

After this episode the learner added L-cmi1-annual-vintage (postmortem:013), visible in later prompt contexts (e.g. runs/adapted/044/workspace/AGENTS.md around line 343).

remedies.intervention: A 'row printings ladder' tool: given a row label, return for every issue the row's cells paired with the resolved column-header text (e.g. 'Calendar Year 2002 r' -> cell) and mark where the value for one period label changes between issues.
remedies.why: The arm's own [41] grep was exactly this ladder minus the headers; with headers attached, the assumption at [44] cannot be made. The cards arm got it right by the equivalent move (grepping the header string 'Calendar Year 2002' across issues at [34]/[39]).

remedies.intervention: Cell-provenance check: every value entering the final computation must be cited as file:line plus the column header; the checker resolves the header from the file, rejects a mismatch with the question's period, and searches later issues for the same header label to report any later printing.
remedies.why: The arm never cited a header for the endpoint; searching later issues for 'Calendar Year 2002' returns 2004_03..2004_09 immediately.

remedies.intervention: Per-table vintage memory retrieved by table id (CM-I-1 annual cells are restated twice; the last printing of CY N is in the March-September issues of N+2).
remedies.why: The learner wrote exactly this lesson after the failure; it only helps when the same table family recurs.

remedies.intervention: Sharper wording: 'a later issue's first column is only a later printing if its header text names the same period; open the header before ruling an issue out'.
remedies.why: The prompt arm already had 'match columns by header, not by position' and still assumed the position.

cards.right_arms_note: Reached the same interim conclusion as the prompt arm at [32] (Dec 2003 = latest), but then grepped the header string 'Calendar Year 2002' across all 2000s issues [34]/[39], found 2004_03..2004_09, and read the 2004_09 header and row at [41]; it explicitly generalized card C003's 'latest issue printing that year' rule from fiscal to calendar years ([32], [42]).

right_arms_note: none and cards both ran one extra search that returned later printings WITH their headers (none: FTS query 'Dec 2002' then reading the 2004_06/2004_03 headers; cards: grep for the header string 'Calendar Year 2002'); prompt ran the same forward search on the row label only and filled in the header by assumption.
text_vs_mechanism: The prompt arm had the right text (vintage self-check, match columns by header) and followed it only partly, so better text alone is a weak fix. A ladder tool that returns header-resolved cells across issues (or a provenance check that resolves headers) would have made the wrong assumption impossible.
notes: A distinctive trap: the first 'r' (revised) printing of an annual column is not final; the same period label persists for three more issues with a second restatement. The signal (identical value repeated across consecutive issues, then changing when the annual column rolls to the next year) was already on screen at [41]. All three arms took similar time (75-97 s); the prompt arm committed right after its first computation, while the right arms spent a few more steps reading headers of later issues.
